title: WPSB/308/2014 of Santosh Kumar Juyal Vs Uttarakhand Public Service Commission AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (SB) No. 308 of 2014
Santosh Kumar Juyal. ........... Petitioner
Versus
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission
& others. ............. Respondents
Mr. Shobhit Saharia, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. B.D. Kandpal, Advocate for respondent No. 1.
Ms. Anjali Bhargava, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand / respondent No. 3.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Dated: 28th April, 2015
K.M. JOSEPH, C.J. (Oral)
 Petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking the following reliefs:
"I. Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of certiorari
quashing the result dated 23.08.2014 qua one person in the
General Category who is shown to be selected on the post of
Deputy Principal / Senior Lecturer etc. as shown in
paragraph / column 12 of the impugned result, who has
obtained lesser marks than the petitioner i.e. Respondent no.
2.
II. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondent no. 1 to declare the petitioner
successful and selected in Uttarakhand Combined State Civil
/ Upper Subordinate Service Exam 2010 on the post of
Deputy Principal / Senior Lecturer etc. as mentioned at
Paragraph / Column 12 of impugned result dated
23.08.2014."
2. An Advertisement was issued by the Public Service Commission
(hereinafter referred to as the "Commission") for filling-up various posts
in the Civil Services. The posts could be, broadly, classified with
reference to the qualifications specified for the same. Some of the posts
required Post Graduation with specialisation. Some of the other posts,
which were advertised, required qualification of Graduation in specialised

2
subject. Lastly, there were posts for which the qualification prescribed
was Graduation or Post Graduation without any specialisation. The
controversy involved in this case, as is evident from the prayers, relates to
the posts of Deputy Principal / Senior Lecturer, etc. For the combined
posts, the selection procedure involved undergoing the preliminary
examination and, thereafter, on being selected, taking of a main
examination and, for those, who are found eligible for interview, the
holding of an interview. The marks obtained in the main examination and
in the interview were to be totalled and a decision was to be made
regarding the result.
3. The complaint of the petitioner would, in essence, be as follows:
 The party respondent secured lesser marks than the petitioner and,
yet, he has been declared selected for the post of Deputy Principal / Senior
Lecturer. It is the further case of the petitioner that, originally, the
Commission had duplicated the roll numbers of the candidates and,
therefore, did not comply with the principle of 1:3. That is to say, as per
law, 15 times the number of posts had to be permitted to sit for the main
examination. The total is 213 posts, for which Graduation or Post
Graduation without specialisation was prescribed. Therefore, 3212
candidates had to be permitted to sit for the main examination.
Thereafter, the yardstick was from among those, who participated in the
main examination, in a ratio of 1:3 for the posts they were to be called for
the interview. This meant that, from among those candidates, who sat in
the main examination, qua each post, the Commission was to call the
candidates in the ratio of 1:3, meaning that, multiplying the number of
posts by 3 and such number of the candidates based on merit from top
down had to be called for interview. There was no minimum requirement
to be fulfilled, by way of minimum marks obtained in the main
examination, to be called for interview. It is, in breach of the aforesaid
criteria, that candidates were called for the interview by duplication of roll
numbers by result declared on 2nd February, 2014. This resulted in

3
litigation and, by a judgment passed in Writ Petition (SB) No. 54 of 2014
(Annexure No. 6), this Court ordered as follows:
"Supplementary counter affidavit, filed by respondent No. 1
in Court, is accepted on record.
2. In the Advertisement, the Commission had indicated
that there are certain posts, which are available for those, who have
academic qualification of Post Graduation. This order is not in
relation to those posts.
3. The Advertisement also mentioned that there are
certain posts, which are available for persons having academic
qualification of Graduation. Out of those posts advertised,
according to the Commission, 38 posts are available for Scheduled
Caste candidates. According to the Commission, out of those 38
posts, some posts are available for Scheduled Caste women
candidates, physically handicapped and other category of
candidates. It has been contended that, according to the Rules
adopted by the Commission, the Commission is required to call for
interview 114 candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste category on
the basis of their merit. The Commission has submitted that, while
calling these candidates, candidates, who were called for the Post
Graduation posts, having also been called for the Graduation posts;
the number of candidates called for Graduation posts is less than
114. In addition to that, it has been contended that, for the posts
reserved for Scheduled Caste women, physically handicapped and
other category of candidates, sufficient number of candidates on the
basis of merit could not be found and, accordingly, the number of
people called for interview was less than 114.
4. The posts, which have been advertised for Post
Graduates, are specialist posts of higher status and with higher
income. A person, who is a Post Graduate, alone, can compete for
the said post. Because he has competed for the said post, he will
not be permitted to compete for the post, where the qualification is
Graduation; is neither the mandate of the Rules nor the mandate of
the Advertisement. The standard of interview for a higher post
cannot be the same for a lower post. Therefore, a Scheduled Caste
candidate, who has been called for interview for the higher post, for
which the basic educational qualification is Post Graduation, while
being interviewed, cannot be assessed, how good he will be for the
post, where the educational qualification is Graduation. Therefore,
a person, who has offered himself for a post, where Post Graduation
is the basic qualification, and also for a post, where the post is for
Graduates; is required to be assessed twice at the interview to be
held for the said posts.
5. In the circumstances, we dispose of this writ petition
by directing the Commission to call 114 candidates belonging to
Scheduled Caste category on the basis of merit at the interview for
the posts, where Graduation is the basic qualification. It is made
clear that, in the event, three times of the number of Scheduled

4
Caste women, physically handicapped and other category of
candidates are not available, then, they be supplied by the ordinary
Scheduled Caste candidates at the interview on the basis of their
merit. In the event, similar mistake has taken place while calling
General candidates / OBC candidates / Scheduled Tribe candidates,
we request the Commission to correct such mistake."
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that, pursuant
thereto, interview was held; but the Commission seizing upon one solitary
sentence in the judgment, has again acted illegally and the petitioner was
not considered for the post of Deputy Principal / Senior Lecturer for
which he was, otherwise, entitled. He was not called for the interview.
5. The case of the Commission, on the other hand, is as follows:
"7. That according to the cut of marks for the interview for
the post of deputy principal / lecturer etc came up 871.9997 marks
whereas the petitioner has scored 866.1566 marks as such he was
not declared qualified for the interview of this post."
6. The Commission also refers to the subsequent litigation. Petitioner
has also filed a rejoinder affidavit.
7. We have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and also the
learned counsel for the Commission.
8. We are, in this case, exclusively concerned only with the posts, for
which, Post Graduation without specialisation is prescribed. We are not
concerned with the posts, for which, Graduation without specialisation, is
prescribed. The litigation, which culminated in Annexure No. 6
judgment, arose as candidates, who were having Post Graduation, were
called and, apparently, they were considered only for the post for which
Post Graduation is required. This is clear from the judgment, where the
Court holds that mere fact that a candidate is having Post Graduation does
not mean that he should not be interviewed for those posts for which,
both, Post Graduation is prescribed and also for which Graduation is
separately prescribed, if they are otherwise eligible. It is, on the said

5
basis, finding that there was non-compliance by the Commission with the
formula of 1:3 qua those posts for which Graduation was prescribed as
there was duplication by calling Post Graduates, that the Court ordered
interview to be held for the post of Graduation. The Court took special
care in the very first paragraph to indicate that this judgment is not meant
for the Post Graduates. We are unable to see how the pertinent
observation made by the Division Bench can be brushed aside as being
the basis for the Commission committing the alleged mischief alleged by
the learned counsel for the petitioner. As noted, petitioner obtained
866.1566 marks in the main examination. The cut off marks mentioned in
the said paragraph is 871.9997. A perusal of the reply affidavit shows
that the contention, which is taken in the pleadings, was that there is no
power to fix such a cut off marks.
9. At this juncture, we must bear in mind, in law, the expression "cut
off marks" has two different connotations. It may appear that the
recruiting body or appointing authority may, faced with large number of
applications, decide to have a cut off marks so as to avoid processing of
unnecessary number of applications. Even though the word "cut off
marks" is used in that sense, it means that only those candidates, who
secure marks which is prescribed as cut off marks either in the
preliminary examination or in the main examination or in the interview,
will be allowed to pass muster. For this, there must definitely be power
and it must also be prescribed earlier. The word "cut of marks" is also
understood in another sense and that is the sense, in which, we think it has
to be understood in this case. "Cut off marks", understood in the latter
sense, means when it is mentioned that the persons, who have either taken
the examination, preliminary or main, will be called for interview in a
particular ratio. "Cut off marks" means the marks, which have been
obtained by the candidate, who occupies the last position calculated for
making up the ratio. It is, in this sense, that the "cut off marks" is
understood and, if it is taken that the petitioner has not obtained the said
cut off marks, as he has obtained marks far less than the cut off marks
going by the averments in paragraph 7 of the counter affidavit, than the

6
stand of the Commission is only to be vindicated. In this connection,
petitioner searched in vain for any averment in the writ petition or
otherwise to the effect that 273 candidates were not called for interview.
The figure 273 represents the number of candidates, who should have
been called for interview qua 91 posts for which Post Graduation without
specialisation was prescribed as the qualification. We say this because the
learned counsel for the petitioner did attempt to make a case that, having
regard to the number of candidates, who were subsequently called
pursuant to the Annexure No. 6 judgment, the number of the candidates
would be more and, therefore, the Court must interfere. In absence of any
pleading that 273 candidates were not called and reading the averments in
the counter affidavit as noted and also the stand, which was taken up in
the rejoinder affidavit, which has not been persevered during the course of
arguments, we are of the view that no case is made out for considering the
reliefs, which are sought in the writ petition.
10. Accordingly, the writ petition fails and is dismissed without costs.
(V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C. J.)
 28.04.2015 28.04.2015
G
